articles.headline: 2027 NBA championship odds: Spurs early favorites to win it all, followed by Thunder and Celtics
articles.description: With the 2025-26 season wrapped up, here's an early look at the odds for the 2027 NBA Finals.

images.name: Spurs [1296x729]
images.caption: The San Antonio Spurs are the early favorites for the 2027 NBA Finals.
images.alt: San Antonio Spurs guard Devin Vassell (24) and guard Stephon Castle (5) and guard De'aaron Fox (4) and forward Victor Wembanyama (1) and guard Dylan Harper (2) walk back on the court in the fourth quarter during game two of the 2026 NBA Finals.

articles.headline: Inside a Knicks celebration a half-century in the making
articles.description: For decades, the Knicks flailed and chased -- for quick fixes, superstars, splashy hires. But then they chose Jalen Brunson, and the rest is history.

images.name: Ernie Johnson and NBA Commissioner Adam Silver presenting Jalen Brunson the NBA Finals MVP Award with Jose Alvarado and owner James Dolan of the New York Knicks after winning Game 5 of the 2026 NBA Finals. [608x342]
images.alt: Ernie Johnson and NBA Commissioner Adam Silver presenting Jalen Brunson the NBA Finals MVP Award with Jose Alvarado and owner James Dolan of the New York Knicks after winning Game 5 of the 2026 NBA Finals.
images.credit: Photo by Rich Storry / ESPN Images

articles.headline: Knicks' victory takes them off the list of longest title droughts
articles.description: Before Saturday night, the last time the Knicks won a title was 1973.

images.name: Rochester Royals [1296x729]
images.caption: The Kings were called the Royals and based out of Rochester the last time they won a title.
images.credit: NBA Photo Library/NBAE via Getty Images

images.name: Chicago Cardinals [1296x729]
images.caption: The last time the Arizona Cardinals won a title, they were still in Chicago.

images.name: Satchel Paige [1296x729]
images.caption: Satchel Paige got a well-deserved World Series win in 1948 with Cleveland.
images.credit: Bruce Bennett Studios via Getty Images Studios/Getty Images

images.name: Maple Leafs [1296x729]
images.caption: The Leafs' last title came when goalies weren't required to wear masks.
images.credit: Bruce Bennett Studios via Getty Images Studios/Getty Images

images.name: The drought is over! The Knicks win their first NBA title since 1973
images.caption: The drought is over! The Knicks win their first NBA title since 1973

articles.headline: Three teams ahead of champion Knicks in 2027 NBA title odds
articles.description: Three teams -- the Spurs, Thunder and Celtics -- have better odds to win the 2027 NBA championship than the Knicks at sportsbooks around the nation.

images.name: Karl-Anthony Towns and Jalen Brunson of the New York Knicks pose for a photo after the game against the San Antonio Spurs during Game 5 of the 2026 NBA Finals on June 13, 2026 at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas.  [1296x729]
images.alt: Karl-Anthony Towns and Jalen Brunson of the New York Knicks pose for a photo after the game against the San Antonio Spurs during Game 5 of the 2026 NBA Finals on June 13, 2026 at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas.

article.story: ORLANDO, Fla. -- — Desmond Bane scored 18 of his 37 points in the fourth quarter, helping the Orlando Magic beat the Chicago Bulls 125-120 on Monday night. Bane made a go-ahead 3-pointer with 3:23 left, sparking an 8-0 run for the Magic. He also capped the decisive sequence with a foul shot that made it 117-111 with 2:11 to go. Bane was 12 for 17 from the field. He also had six rebounds and five assists. Franz Wagner scored 25 points for Orlando, and reserve Anthony Black had 22 points and nine rebounds. The Magic won for the sixth time in seven games. Josh Giddey had 22 points, nine rebounds and six assists for Chicago in its fourth consecutive loss. Matas Buzelis scored 21 points, and Nikola Vucevic had 20 points and 11 rebounds. The Bulls led by as many as 15 points in the third quarter, holding the Magic without a field goal for the first five minutes of the period. But Bane made a 3-pointer and Noah Penda had a driving dunk that tied it at 85 going into the fourth. Wendell Carter Jr. scored 17 points for Orlando on 6-for-8 shooting. Tre Jones had 20 points for Chicago, and Ayo Dosunmu finished with 18 points and seven assists. Up next Bulls: Host the Brooklyn Nets on Wednesday night. Magic: Continue their three-game homestand on Wednesday night against the San Antonio Spurs. ------ AP NBA: https://apnews.com/hub/nba
